account:
Today has largely followed my appointments: morning office business and market walk, lunch at home, town accounts, and tea with my neighbour at the east-bank dockside cottage. I am leaving tea to return to the office for 16:30. The secretary reports no correspondence, accounts figures, expenses, or requests for decisions submitted today. I requested a financial summary and a record of local news.

The only unusual report is a vague rumour of a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' My neighbour attributes those words to Townsfolk Two, outside the bakery this morning. When pressed, the reported observations were simply the baker carrying wheat and lights at the bakery. I also heard Townsfolk 30 report the baker carrying wheat. My neighbour says the baker denied any special occasion and described his work as ordinary fresh bread for the market. I have not personally witnessed a project, unusual gathering, or interesting visitor; my neighbour says they have not seen such gatherings or visitors by the docks today either.

At present I cannot establish that anything secret or unusual is happening. Wheat deliveries and lights could readily be normal baking activity, and the rumour may be a misunderstanding. Townsfolk Two is the person to ask for a firsthand explanation if I investigate further. Separately, my neighbour suggested a bench by the landing for sitting and greeting neighbours; that is their own wish, not evidence of an existing riverside project.
